card.name: Quadrille
card.tagline: Napoleon's ballroom dance for four couples — the French square-formation that became American square dance and Caribbean creolized national dances.
card.profile: The quadrille is a dance that was fashionable in late 18th- and 19th-century Europe and its colonies. The quadrille consists of a chain of four to six contredanses. Latterly the quadrille was frequently danced to a medley of opera melodies. Performed by four couples in a rectangular formation, it is related to American square dancing. The quadrille also gave rise to Cape Breton Square Dancing via American square dancing in New England.
card.insight: The dance was introduced in France around 1760: originally it was a form of cotillion in which only two couples were used, but two more couples were eventually added to form the sides of a square. Reaching English high society in 1816 through Lady Jersey, the quadrille became a craze.
